# `silk/testing/selection`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

How the built-in test runner skips a passing test whose code and inputs did not change.

## When to use
`silk.testing.runner` uses this module. You do not call it from normal code.

## Details
A test runner that `silk test` builds for an ELF or Mach-O target holds a table of every
function in it: for each one a flag, which the function sets when it starts, and the digest of
everything the compiler read to make it. [`Table`](#Table) reads that table. Before a test runs, the
runner clears the flags; after it, the set flags are the functions the test executed.

The runner also watches the test (`silk.testing.observation`): the files, directory listings and
environment variables it read, and whether it used the clock, randomness, the network or a child
process.

A record file keeps, for each test that passed, the digests of the functions it executed and a
digest of each input it read, taken after it ran. A later run skips the test when every one of
those functions is in the new runner with the same digest and every input reads the same. A
test that executes the same functions on the same inputs does the same thing, so it passes
again.

A test is not recorded, so it runs every time, when it failed, when it used the clock,
randomness, the network or a child process, listed the environment, read more than the watch
holds, or executed a function the compiler gave no digest, as in a build without a cache.

The record starts with the magic `SLKTREC1` and a version, then the runner's table: its count
and each function's 16-byte digest. Then the working directory, and for each recorded test its
identity, the table positions of its functions as increasing LEB128 differences, and its inputs:
kind, root, path and a 32-byte SHA-256. Integers are little-endian `u64`; text is a `u64` length
and its bytes.

## Gotchas
- Work a process does once, such as filling a cache on first use, is recorded only for the test
  that did it. A later test that relies on it can be skipped after an edit to that work.
- A test that reads the host other than through the native providers reads unseen.

Import as `TestSelection` with `import silk.testing.selection as TestSelection`.

<a id="Table.impl.between"></a>

### Associated function `between`

```silk
pub unsafe fn between(start: ?*const u8, stop: ?*const u8) -> Table
```

The table that lies between `start` and `stop`, the bounds of the section that holds the
records of a test runner's functions. It is empty when either is null or `stop` is not
after `start`.

#### Details
A test runner that `silk test` builds for an ELF or Mach-O target holds the records in the
section `silk_seen` (`__DATA,__silk_seen` on Mach-O), whose bounds the linker names
`__start_silk_seen` and `__stop_silk_seen`. Each record is 17 bytes: a flag the function sets
when it starts, then its 16-byte content digest.

#### Safety
The bytes between the bounds must be such records, writable, and stay valid while the table
is used.

<a id="digestInput"></a>

## `digestInput`

```silk
pub effect fn digestInput(kind: u8, root: &[u8], path: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator | &mut HostInput
```

The SHA-256 of what the input of `kind` at `path`, through a provider rooted at `root`, reads
now: a file's contents, an entry's kind and size, a directory's names, or a variable's value,
each after a word for its kind, or a word for a failure.

<a id="inputs"></a>

## `inputs`

```silk
pub effect fn inputs(notes: &[u8]) -> Option<List<Input>> ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator | &mut HostInput
```

The inputs the notes of a watch buffer `notes` name, each once, with their digests now, or
`None` when the test cannot be recorded.

### Details
Notes under a directory the test created with a unique name ([`Observation.TEMPORARY`](./testing-observation.md#TEMPORARY)) are
the test's own and name no input. A change to any other path ([`Observation.WRITE`](./testing-observation.md#WRITE)) means a
later run would start from what the test left, so the result is `None`. So is a buffer whose
notes do not parse.
